title: Platform systems & services — playbook, runbooks, dashboards, roadmap, and retrospective (Q1 2026)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This page consolidates the platform engineering playbook for core systems and services: inventory, ownership, SLOs, dashboards and alerting, production runbooks, Q1 2026 retrospective highlights, and the roadmap for the next quarter. Intended audience: oncall engineers, SREs, platform owners, and product stakeholders.

Table of contents:
1) Introduction and goals
2) Systems & services inventory (summary)
3) Ownership, SLOs, and escalation paths
4) Dashboards & alerts (what to watch)
5) Critical runbooks (triage + remediation)
6) Q1 2026 retrospective: incidents, root causes, and action items
7) Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)
8) How-to / troubleshooting tips and CLI snippets
9) References and related pages

1) Introduction and goals
The platform team provides the shared services required to run Redwood inference reliably and cost-effectively. This document is the canonical playbook: a single place for runbooks, dashboard definitions, SLO ownership, and short-term roadmap priorities. Goals for this document:
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-restore for service-impacting incidents.
- Provide clear ownership for automated remediation and follow-up work.
- Align Q2 roadmap items with the top operational risks identified in Q1 2026.

2) Systems & services inventory (summary)
Below is a concise inventory of the highest-priority platform systems. For each service, the full component-level diagram is linked in the team wiki.
| Service name | Purpose | Primary owner | SLO (target) | Pager? | Runbook link |
|-------------|---------|---------------|--------------|--------|--------------|
| inference-runtime | Token-level text generation and chat inference (hosted) | infra-serving | 99.95% availability; 95th pct latency < 150ms | yes | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-incident-runbook-2025 |
| autoscaler | Cluster autoscaling for dedicated pools | infra-platform | Scale latency 99% < 60s from signal | yes | /confluence/eng-platform/autoscaler-runbook-2025 |
| kv-cache (redis) | Prefix/KV cache for generations | infra-caching | Error rate < 0.1% | yes | /confluence/eng-platform/kv-cache-runbook-2026 |
| request-router | Smart routing, fallbacks, and cost-routing | infra-routing | Correct routing % >= 99.9% | yes | /confluence/eng-platform/router-runbook-2026 |
| metrics-collector | Ingest and export platform telemetry | infra-observability | Data retention 30 days, ingestion success > 99.5% | no | /confluence/eng-platform/metrics-collector-ops |

3) Ownership, SLOs, and escalation paths
- Primary owners: listed above. Secondary (backup) owners are listed in the team wiki.
- SLO targets are expressed as availability or latency percentiles. SLO burn policy: if an SLO incurs > 5% error budget burn in a 30-day window, we trigger an SLO review (owner + SRE).
- Escalation matrix: first-page (primary oncall) -> 15 minutes. If unresolved after 30 minutes escalate to platform lead. For cross-team impact (eg: storage, networking), notify the relevant product owner and customer-success.

4) Dashboards & alerts (what to watch)
High-level dashboards (links to Grafana panels):
- Platform: "Platform Overview" (panels: cluster CPU/GPU utilization, cluster free memory, request qps, 95th/99th latency by model).
- Inference: "Inference Latency by Model" (95th/99th), "Token Errors" (token-level parse failures).
- Autoscaler: "Scaling events" (time-to-scale, pending pods), "Failed scale ops".
- Cache: "Redis latency and evictions".
- Routing: "Mismatch rate" (requests sent to fallback models).

Critical alerts and thresholds (examples):
- inference-runtime-high-latency: 99th latency > 600ms for 5m -> P1. Pager to inference oncall. Runbook: see 'Inference: high tail latency' below.
- inference-runtime-error-rate: 5xx rate > 0.5% over 3m -> P1.
- autoscaler-failed-scaling: scale errors >= 3 in 10m -> P2.
- redis-eviction-spike: eviction rate > 1000/s or mem_used > 85% -> P1.
- metrics-ingest-drop: ingestion success < 98% over 10m -> P2.

Alert routing: alerts go to #oncall-platform Slack and OpsDuty. Pager rotations defined in team wiki. Alert runbook link is included in each alert's description in Grafana/Alertmanager.

5) Critical runbooks (triage + remediation)
A. Inference: high tail latency (P1)
Steps to triage:
1) Acknowledge the page in OpsDuty and post to #oncall-platform with initial summary (time, affected region, sample request IDs).
2) Confirm scope: check Grafana panels for 95th/99th latency and QPS by model. Use the query:
   curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))" | jq .
3) Check GPUs: run kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide and nvidia-smi on affected nodes:
   kubectl exec -n infra-serving $(kubectl get pods -n infra-serving -l app=inference-runtime -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- nvidia-smi
4) Check KV-cache hit rate: Grafana panel "KV cache hit rate" and redis-cli INFO. If hit rate < 70% and QPS unchanged, consider cache miss storm — apply temporary cache bypass for heavy prompts.
5) If CPU/GPU saturation found, trigger autoscaler manual scale:
   kubectl scale deployment inference-runtime --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deployment inference-runtime -n infra-serving -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}') + 2)) -n infra-serving
6) If a model rollout correlates with latency spike, route traffic to previous stable model version via request-router admin console (roll back canary).
Remediation notes: prioritize restoration over full root-cause analysis. Capture all steps in the incident ticket.

B. Redis (kv-cache) OOMs or large eviction spikes (P1)
1) Acknowledge page and post to Slack.
2) Check redis metrics: redis_memory_used_bytes, redis_evicted_keys_total.
3) If memory > 90% or evictions > 1000/s: increase redis_maxmemory for the cluster shard or fail open cache for <5% of traffic.
   redis-cli -h $HOST CONFIG SET maxmemory "18gb"
4) If persistent OOM, restart the shard with node draining:
   kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets <node> && kubectl delete pod <redis-pod> -n infra-caching
5) Postmortem checklist: identify workload causing the spike (large prefixes, mis-configured keys), add rate limiting or TTL enforcement.

C. Autoscaler failed to scale (P2 -> escalate to P1 if service impact)
1) Check the autoscaler logs in EKS/GKE and internal controller metrics.
2) Validate cloud account quotas (EC2/GPU GPUS) and check cloud provider events.
3) If cloud quota exhausted, open escalation with cloudops and re-route traffic to lower-tier region or model.
4) Temporary mitigation: manually add capacity pool or reduce model parallelism.

6) Q1 2026 retrospective: incidents, root causes, and action items
Summary of major incidents:
- 2026-01-12: Inference tail latency incident (3.5 hours). Root cause: a canary model with a change to KV encoding caused cache misses and increased memory pressure on GPUs. Action items: add preflight canary perf tests (owner: infra-serving, target: 2026-04-15), add canary SLO gates for 95/99 latency, and enable canary traffic cap (owner: infra-routing).
- 2026-02-02: Redis shard eviction storm (1.2 hours). Root cause: a customer workload wrote large unbounded keys. Action items: implement per-customer write quotas to cache and TTL defaults (owner: infra-caching, ETA: 2026-05-01).
- 2026-02-18: Autoscaler misconfiguration during a deployment (45m). Root cause: controller ignored pending pods due to label mismatch. Action items: add unit/integration test for label semantics in autoscaler and add test into CI (owner: infra-platform, ETA: 2026-03-20).
Follow-up backlog (top priorities):
- Preflight performance harness for model rollouts (infra-serving).
- Add cache write quotas and TTL enforcement (infra-caching).
- Improve alerting noise: adjust thresholds to reduce P2 noise by 40% (observability team).

7) Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)
High-level goals for Q2 2026:
- Observability maturity: add 90/99/99.9 latency quantiles for all models, synthetic traffic canaries, and improved dashboard drilldowns. (owner: infra-observability, ETA: 2026-04-30).
- Autoscaler resilience: controller retries, label-sanitization tests, and capacity pool warmers. (owner: infra-platform, ETA: 2026-05-30).
- Cost and performance tooling: deploy initial Redwood Optimize recommendations integration for platform-authored workloads. (owner: infra-serving + product, ETA: 2026-06-15).
- Ops playbook improvements: expand runbooks, table top drills, and add guided oncall run-throughs quarterly. (owner: eng-platform, ETA: 2026-04-20).
Milestones (quarterly):
- Apr 2026: Canary perf harness delivered; initial synthetic canaries configured.
- May 2026: Autoscaler resilience changes live in staging; CI tests added.
- Jun 2026: Cache quotas and TTL rules implemented for high-risk customers.

8) How-to / troubleshooting tips and CLI snippets
Common queries and commands:
- Query 99th latency for a model (Prometheus):
  curl -g 'https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="gpt-open-7b"}) by (le))' | jq .
- Check pod resource usage (kubectl + metrics server):
  kubectl top pods -n infra-serving --selector=app=inference-runtime
- Temporarily route 10% traffic away from canary model (request-router CLI):
  routerctl set-split --route inference --model canary-2026-02 --percent 10
- Alertmanager silence creation (CLI):
  amtool silence add --duration=1h "maintenance" -m "team=infra-platform"
Example alert rule (Prometheus-format YAML snippet):
  - alert: InferenceHighTailLatency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 0.6
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "99th percentile inference latency > 600ms for 5m"

9) References and related pages
- Platform team wiki (detailed ownership and component diagrams): /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026.json
- Runtime incident runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-incident-runbook-2025.json
- Autoscaler runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/autoscaler-runbook-2025.json

Appendix: post-incident checklist (to attach to the incident ticket)
1) Timeline: collect logs + traces for 1 hour before and after the incident start time.
2) Metrics snapshot: export all affected Grafana panels to PNG and attach.
3) Root-cause hypothesis + validated root cause.
4) Action owner and ETA for each corrective item.
5) Communication: reflect incident summary in the weekly ops review and notify customer-success for any customer impact.

If you are oncall and unsure, call the platform lead (Ethan Chen) or follow the quick-runbook card pinned in #oncall-platform.
